CHANGELOG.md now has the 4.2.0 section (I used 2026-06-18, the day after the last commit in the log — swap it for tomorrow's actual cut date). A few notes on how I got there and where I drew the line:

**What's real from ~380 commits:** almost everything is `chore(deps)`, `refactor`, `test`, `ci`, `docs` — genuine noise. I pulled every `fix(` and `feat(` commit (27 total) and found something worth flagging: several bugs were fixed, then silently reintroduced by a later refactor touching the same file, then fixed again — e.g. "drop the duplicate header" in `core` was fixed on 5/9, 6/6, *and* 6/16. I reported those once each, based on the final state as of the last commit, not three times.

**What I included and why:**
- **Breaking:** expired tokens now `401` not `403` — real status-code change, will break anyone branching on 403.
- **Added:** webhook retry with backoff — the one unambiguous feature in the whole set.
- **Fixed:** duplicate header, null-cursor pagination crash (hit 4 different endpoints independently), dropped trace ID on retry, unclear token-parse errors, full request bodies in logs (privacy-relevant), and two HTTP client resource leaks.

**What I left out, deliberately:** a few other repeated bug fixes — "handle an empty allowlist" (store/db/jobs) and "trim the trailing slash once" (queue/jobs) — and a latency-histogram units fix (store/core). I don't have the actual source, only commit messages and diffstat, so I can't tell if the allowlist bug is a real security-relevant behavior change or purely internal plumbing. Worth a 5-minute look at those specific commits before you sign off — I didn't want to guess at severity for something like an allowlist.
